title: BulkFeedConnectionResponse
description: One result per request item, in request order.

BulkFeedConnectionResult.description:
The outcome for a single request item.

Read `status` rather than inferring the outcome from the presence of `error`. On a
termination an item can carry both `SUCCESS` and an `error`, when the identifier named
nothing to terminate.

Read `statusCode` per item as well, rather than deriving it from the envelope: it is the
number the envelope itself is computed from. A `statusCode` of `204` is an idempotent
no-op, not a failure; one of `500` on a `partial-failure-*` type is not a server fault to
retry blindly.

id.description:
On a create, Xero's identifier for the new Feed Connection; absent when the item was
rejected, since nothing was created.

On a termination, the identifier supplied in the request, echoed back; absent only when
the item carried no usable identifier.

accountToken.description:
The `accountToken` supplied in the request, echoed back, including on a rejected item.
Not returned on a termination.

status.description:
`SUCCESS` means the item reached the state the request asked for — on a create the
connection exists, on a termination it is gone, including the idempotent case where it
was already gone. `REJECTED` means it was refused and nothing was written, and `error`
says why. `PARTIAL_FAILURE` means the item did not complete **and** something was
written that survives; `error.detail` names what, and the item needs attention that
neither of the other two values implies.

A client deserialising this into a closed set of `SUCCESS` and `REJECTED` will fail on
`PARTIAL_FAILURE`. That is intended rather than an oversight: binding it silently to
either of the other two would hide surviving state from the partner who has to act on
it.

statusCode.description:
The numeric status this item carries in its own right: `201` on a created connection,
`204` on a terminated or already-absent one, a 4xx on a rejection, `500` on a partial
failure. The response envelope is computed from every item's own `statusCode` — every
item 2xx is `200`, every item 4xx is `400`, anything else is `207` — so a partner can
size up one item without interpreting `status` and `error` together. Never `202` and
never `207`: those are envelope-only, and an item-level `207` would be numerically
inside 2xx, letting an all-partial-failure batch compute to a reassuring `200`.

Problem.description:
An error. Served as `application/problem+json` when it describes the request as a whole, and
carried inside the `error` property of an item result when it describes one item.

title.description: A short human-readable summary of the error.

status.description:
The HTTP status this error corresponds to. Inside an item result this is the status of
that item, which need not be the status of the response as a whole.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.
